rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hostility toward the Prophet because of his religion is more severe kufr than merely failing to believe; enacted hostility is war, and spoken hostility is abuse.
rows.anchor: ile buğz u adâvet, ona iman etmemekten ibaret olan küfürden ehas, daha şiddetli bir küfürdür.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Actual enmity amounts to declaring war, while verbal enmity is insult; the sharia makes such insult liable to war and death.
rows.anchor: Bunun fiilen izhârı ona fiilen harb ilânı olacağı gibi kavlen izhârı da o mânada olarak sebb ü şetm olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic causal wording after the command to pray and sacrifice signals that the hater is the one truly cut off.
rows.anchor: وَٱنْحَرْ emrinden sonra tahkik ile beraber illiyet de ifade eden اِنَّ ile ta‘lîl siyâkında إِنَّ شَانِئَكَ هُوَ ٱلْأَبْتَرُ buyurulmasında

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who slander the Prophet deserve to be cut off and left wholly without lasting good, becoming infamous; the Prophet's good and influence will endure.
rows.anchor: sonunda kesilmeye müstahik olduklarına işaret ve hatta sonlarında bir hayırları kalmayıp büsbütün bednâm olacaklarını ihtar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told not to grieve but to worship, pray, sacrifice, and show gratitude for his Lord's gift through sacrifice for good.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah’ın keder etmeyip de Rabbinin atâsına şükretmek üzere ibadet ve ubûdiyet ile iştigal ederek namaz kılıp kurban kesmesi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the taunt referred to the death of male children, al-abtar first implies that the Prophet's descendants will not be cut off; daughters and their descendants count as his progeny.
rows.anchor: Peygamber’in zürriyetinin de kesilmeyeceği ilk evvel anlaşılması lâzım gelen bir mâna olduğu için, bundan kız evlâdı ve onların evlâdı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's sons did not live to adulthood despite his having several; their early deaths have a wisdom tied to his being the Seal of the Prophets.
rows.anchor: müte‘addid erkek evlâdı da olmuş iken bunların muammer olmayıp

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If his sons survived, prophethood after the final Prophet would be impossible, while survival without prophethood would prevent them from fully succeeding him in honor; their innocent deaths were holier.
rows.anchor: onların masum olarak vefatları hem kendi haklarında hem de şân-ı risalet hakkında

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The continuation of his mission, spread of Islam, and growth of the community benefit the umma and raise the Prophet's reward, while hereditary succession to leadership would conflict with the mission's universal merit-based principles and risk discord.
rows.anchor: imamet velâyetini ehliyetten ziyade neseb verâsetine hasretmek olacağından bu inhisar da bi‘set-i Muhammediyenin umûmiyetine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since prophethood and imamate do not apply to women, those succession-related objections do not arise for the Prophet's daughters.
rows.anchor: Kadınlarda ise nübüvvet ve imamet kaziyyesi esasen vârid olmadığı için kızları hakkında bu mahzurlar vârid olmaz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rational wisdom is that there is no prophethood after him and leadership is not confined to hereditary succession, rather than that daughters' descendants fail to count as progeny.
rows.anchor: Kendisinden sonra nübüvvet olmaması, imamet ve velâyetin de verâset-i nesebiyeye hasredilmemesi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final verse contains a report about the unseen.
rows.anchor: belli ki bu son âyet gayba ta‘alluk eden ihbârı da müştemildir.

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Razi reads the surah through three ranks for spiritual wayfarers: absorption in divine light, bodily worship, and restraining the self from immediate sensual pleasure.
rows.anchor: Râzî tefsirinde bunun Ve’d-Duhâ’dan beri gelen sûrelere olan münasebâtıyla

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Razi associates al-Kawthar with the holy spirit's superiority to other human spirits in quantity of premises and speed and quality of inference.
rows.anchor: de o mukaddimâttan neticelere intikalde sâir rûhlardan çok daha serî‘olmasıdır.

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Razi reads prayer as the second spiritual rank, bodily obedience and worship.
rows.anchor: فَصَلِّ لِرَبِّكَ İkinci mertebeye işaret

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Razi reads sacrifice as the third rank because it restrains the self from immediate pleasures.
rows.anchor: وَٱنْحَرْ da üçüncü mertebeye işarettir, çünkü nefsi peşin lezzetlerinden men‘etmek

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: In Razi's allegory, the self that summons one to sensory desires is transient, whereas enduring righteous deeds are better and spiritual joy and divine knowledge last forever.
rows.anchor: Seni şu mahsüsât ile şehevât-ı âcileye davet eyleyen nefis yok mu, o fânîdir; bâkıyât-ı sâlihât ise Rabbin indinde daha hayırlıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the commands in al-Kawthar emphasize exclusive devotion to the Lord, al-Kafirun follows to state tawhid and sincerity explicitly.
rows.anchor: Bu sûrenin mutazammın olduğu emirlerin en mühim ciheti لِرَبِّكَ kaydının ifade ettiği tevhid ve ihlâs olduğu için

none: Turkish translation of the verses only.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi counts about forty subtleties in beginning with qul; Elmalili highlights that the opening command makes the message an explicit divine commission, not a personal statement by Muhammad.
rows.anchor: En birincisi Hazret-i Peygamber’in kendi tarafından değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Muhammad was commanded to gentleness and wise invitation, the command to convey everything revealed requires him to deliver this severe address as a divine charge.
rows.anchor: burada ise muhatablarına “ey kâfirler!” diye en ağır vasıf ile nidâ edeceği

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them disbelievers names their unchanging trait and prevents an objection that the harsh address violates commands of gentleness; its placement after al-Kawthar also links both commands and their enduring hostility.
rows.anchor: “bunu ben kendiliğimden söylemiyorum, me’mur olarak söylüyorum” demiş olmak için evvelâ قُلْ emri tasrih edilmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence links the opponents' fixed kufr with their hostility and with their contradictory proposal to worship God only if the Prophet also worships their idols.
rows.anchor: ileri sürmeleri de musır oldukları o buğz u şeneânın bir neticesi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Major exegetes limit the address to particular Quraysh disbelievers whom God knew would never believe; a general address would wrongly include People of the Book and future believers.
rows.anchor: ecille-i müfessirîn demişlerdir ki: Burada böyle “ey kâfirler!” diye nidâ ale’l-umûm kâfir bulunanlara değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address can signify all who persist in fixed hostility, but its practical application is confined to the original Quraysh addressees because only God knows who will later believe; it does not license insulting other disbelievers.
rows.anchor: bu hitâbın hâricen fiiliyyât itibariyle tatbîki Kureyş içinde sebeb-i nüzul olanlara münhasır kalmış

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's continuing general use is inward and outward disavowal of unbelief, shirk, and hypocrisy, strengthening sincere faith through recitation as self-admonition rather than attack on others or mere historical memory.
rows.anchor: hükmü küfür ve nifaktan teberrî için gizli, açık her hâlde tilâvettir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophetic hadith recommends reciting it while sleeping as a word that saves from shirk, expressing the surah's devotional purpose.
rows.anchor: Hadîs-i nebevîde şirkten kurtaracak bir kelime olmak üzere uyku sırasında okunmasının tavsiye buyurulması

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This disavowal does not displace general duties of worship, religious detail, good debate, or jihad, and it neither commands attacks on all disbelievers nor forbids debate or struggle.
rows.anchor: Bunun böyle olması ise mücahedeye ve ibadet ve dinin tafsîlâtına dair olan ahkâm-ı umûmiyesine müte‘allik vezâif ile iştigāle mâni‘de olmaz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abrogation would follow only if the final verse instituted an accepted truce or absolute permission; neither reading holds, so no abrogation of general law is needed.
rows.anchor: dinlerinde serbestlikleri esası üzerine bir mütareke teklîfi mâhiyetinde ise onlar kabul etmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alleged truce was never accepted; even if acceptance were assumed, the opponents broke it and attempted to kill the Prophet, so no operative compact needed abrogation.
rows.anchor: asla kabul edilmemiş veya nakz edilmiş bulunan bir mukavelenin bir hükmü farzolunamaz ki neshine hâcet olsun.

rows.speaker: Âlûsî
rows.claim: Alusi warns that the surah is sound in every respect and contains no abrogated ruling.
rows.anchor: Âlûsî’nin de ihtar ettiği gibi bu sûre her vechile muhkemdir, bunda nesholunmuş bir hüküm yoktur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some interpreters say the final clause was abrogated by the sword verses, assuming a universal address and an unconditional truce; Elmalili says such a truce would make sense only if accepted.
rows.anchor: sonundaki لَكُمْ دِينُكُمْ fıkrasının seyf âyetleriyle mensuh olduğunu söyleyenler de olmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening call itself signals struggle, and the final clause is a threat or disavowal like 41:40 and 2:256, not permission; without an initial truce there is nothing to abrogate.
rows.anchor: قُلْ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْكَٰفِرُونَ emri her şeyden evvel bir mücahede telkin eder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No verse in the surah is abrogated; addressing all unbelievers would require specifying the middle verses, so the particular reading is preferable.
rows.anchor: Yalnız evvelâ umûma hamledildiği takdirde ikinci ve üçüncü âyetlerle tahsis iktizâ edeceğine göre bu sebeple îzah olunduğu üzere husûsa hamli evlâdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad refuses both now and later to worship the objects the opponents worship and want him to accept as gods.
rows.anchor: ben ibadet ve ubûdiyet etmem. Buna karşı onların “biz Allah’a da ibadet ederiz” diyebilmeleri ihtimâlini def‘etmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opponents cannot truly worship Muhammad's God because genuine worship requires sincerity and belief in God's oneness; associating partners or imagining another as God is not worship of Him.
rows.anchor: şartı ihlâstır, Allah’ın birliğine iman etmeyince O’na ibadet edilmez.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even when polytheists think they worship God, they worship their own imaginings and desires; the Qur'an asks whether the ignorant would command worship of anyone besides God.
rows.anchor: müşrikler Allah’a ibadet ediyoruz zannetseler bile ibadet etmiş olmazlar, kendi hayâl ve hevâlarına taparlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The switch from present ma ta'budun to past ma abadtum indicates that Muhammad never participated in their past worship either.
rows.anchor: İbtidâen muzâri‘sîgasıyla مَا تَعْبُدُونَ, burada mâzî sîgasıyla مَّا عَبَدتُّمْ buyurulması, onların hâlde olduğu gibi mâzîdeki ta‘abbüdlerine de Peygamber’in iştirak etmemiş olduğuna işaret eder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some grammarians take the active participle abid as carrying past meaning, making the denial cover all time; its ability to govern a direct object with past meaning is disputed.
rows.anchor: bundan dolayı bazıları buradaki أَعْبُدُ ism-i fâilinin mâzî mânasına olduğunu söylemişlerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If ma is a verbal noun, abid can govern it as an absolute object without requiring present or future meaning: Muhammad never performed their shirk worship and never will.
rows.anchor: çünkü o zaman mef‘ûl-i mutlak olabilir, bunda amel için ise hâl veya istikbal mânası şart değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the verbal-noun reading, the verse denies ever adopting their idolatrous practice, whether in the past or at any time to come.
rows.anchor: Ben sizin tapışınızı, o şirk ibadetini hiçbir zaman tapıcı değilim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final denial says the opponents have never, do not, and will not perform Muhammad's worship, or his worship in tawhid and sincerity.
rows.anchor: etmediniz, etmiyorsunuz ve etmezsiniz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view treats the last two denials as emphasis: the nominal third clause strengthens the first, the fourth strengthens the second; Ferrā cites Arabic repetition for emphasis and comprehension and compares 102:3-4.
rows.anchor: Ferrâ buna zâhib olmuş ve demiştir ki: “Kur’an Arab lügatıyla nâzil olmuştur, tekid ve ifham için kelâmı tekrar etmek de onların âdetlerindendir

rows.speaker: Tîbî
rows.claim: Tibi adopts the interpretation that the repeated clauses chiefly reinforce and sever the opponents' hope of ever believing.
rows.anchor: Tîbî[^19] de bunu ihtiyar eylemiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphasis account faces a syntactic objection: coordinated clauses do not ordinarily serve as emphasis except with thumma; allowing waw requires analogy and separating emphasized material with unrelated clauses is grammatically problematic.
rows.anchor: Lâkin, burada atıf vardır; hâlbuki cümlelerin tekidi ثُمَّ’den başka âtıf ile olmaz diye itiraz edilmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority hold that these clauses introduce distinct meanings, not mere repetition, because tense, continuation, ma's function, and context allow many contrasts.
rows.anchor: cumhur bu âyetlerde mânen tekrar olmadığını ve binâen‘aleyh sade tekid değil, her birinin bir tesis olduğunu beyan eylemişlerdir.

rows.speaker: Keşşâf
rows.claim: Kashshaf reads the first pair as denial of future requested worship, the third as denial of any past idolatry, and the fourth as denial that the opponents ever worshipped Muhammad's God; Ebussuud chooses this view.
rows.anchor: Keşşâf şöyle demiştir: “Mâna: Ben müstakbelde benden istediğinizi, o ilâhlarınıza ibadeti yapmam

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Kashshaf's analysis the first two clauses deny future acts, the third can deny the past circumstantially, and the fourth gives a comprehensive negation across time.
rows.anchor: Bu suretle her cümlenin ayrı bir mâna ifade etmesinin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kashshaf's future-only reading is defended because the demand concerned the future and la abudu commonly denies the future, then the rhetoric escalates through past to all time.
rows.anchor: maksad hasr olmayıp sebeb-i nüzulde taleb, istikbâle ait olduğundan ve لَآ أَعْبُدُ nefy-i istikbalde meşhur bulunduğundan dolayı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kisai accepts a past active participle governing a direct object, while most grammarians reject it; this makes attributing the grammar to Kashshaf doubtful.
rows.anchor: Kisâî bunu kabul etmiş ise de cumhur reddederler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalili allows the past nuance of abid from the past abadtum form while retaining present and future meanings, either by morphological correspondence or by reading ma as a verbal noun; the latter yields a comprehensive, emphatic new denial.
rows.anchor: O hâlde amel ya bazılarının dediği gibi mâkabline müşâkele suretiyledir, yahut مَا ibadet mânasına hamledilmek itibariyle masdariyye gibi mef‘ûl-i mutlak menzilesinde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Variations in verb forms, ma, and waw create many interpretive nuances; Turkish lacks a present-tense relative clause, so the translation taptığınız obscures whether the Arabic is present or past.
rows.anchor: Ancak şunu da söyleyelim ki مَا تَعْبُدُونَ، مَٓا اَعْبُدُ fiilleri hâldir, bunların gerek mevsul ve gerek masdariyyet üzere tercemelerinde biz hâl mânasını açık ve kısa olarak ifade edemiyoruz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opponents' worship is explicitly marked both present and past, while the Prophet's past worship is implicit; this stresses that the model to follow is his worship since prophethood began.
rows.anchor: Peygamber’e ait olanda sade أَنتُمْ عَٰبِدُونَ diye hâl fiili tasrih olunmuş, mâzî zımnen geçilmiş olmasında mühim bir nükte vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Your religion means your established kufr and shirk, with its responsibility, accounting, punishment, and burden belonging wholly to you; Muhammad is wholly clear of it and they should not expect his acceptance.
rows.anchor: bütün mes’ûliyeti, hesâbı, cezâsı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most exegetes take the verse as confirming the preceding refusals; Muhammad's religion is Islam, worship in tawhid and sincerity, and its reward and al-Kawthar belong to him, not his opponents.
rows.anchor: Müfessirînin ekserîsi demişlerdir ki: Bu لَكُمْ دِينُكُمْ yukarıki لَآ أَعْبُدُ مَا تَعْبُدُونَ kavliyle وَلَآ أَنَا۠ عَابِدٌۭ مَّا عَبَدتُّمْ kavlini takrirdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spelling dinukum reflects deletion of the first-person ya of dini, with the kasra retained in its place.
rows.anchor: دِينُكُمْ Aslı د۪ين۪يِ’dir, kesre ile iktifâ olunarak mütekellim yâ’sı hazf edilmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the contrast as their kufr belonging to them and his tawhid and sincerity belonging to him; this does not permit kufr, since the Prophet was sent to forbid it.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas demiştir ki: Allah’a küfrünüz sizin, O’na tevhid ve ihlâs da benim, o hâlde onların küfürlerine izin verilmiş denilebilir mi? Hayır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi's quoted explanations also understand the line as a threat, a demand that opponents stop inviting the Prophet to shirk after rejecting his call, or a warning that he will not abandon his religion even if theirs leads to ruin.
rows.anchor: Birincisi: Bundan maksud ٱعْمَلُوا۟ مَا شِئْتُمْ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi records din as account: each side answers for its own deeds, with no liability for the other's actions.
rows.anchor: ‘Din’ hesabdır. ‘Sizin hesâbınız size, benim hesâbım banadır, hiçbirimizin amelinden diğerine bir mes’ûliyet teveccüh etmez’ demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi records din as recompense: their punishment for their religion is theirs, while the reward and honor of the Prophet's religion are his.
rows.anchor: ‘Din’den murad cezâsı, üzerine terettüb edecek ikāb veya sevabdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi records din as a prescribed penalty or hadd, warning the opponents to fear their Lord's punishment while Muhammad need not fear the idols' impotent punishment.
rows.anchor: Burada da ukūbet mânasınadır (bu, ‘cezâ’ mânasından ehastır, Türkçemizde kullandığımız ‘cezâ’ demektir).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi records din as supplication: their invocations belong to them but are futile, idols cannot hear or answer and disown their shirk on Judgment Day, while God answers believers.
rows.anchor: dua mânasına gelir. Yani sizin duanız, yalvarmanız sizin olsun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi records din as custom: their inherited Satanic idolatrous custom is theirs, while the Prophet follows the custom revealed by God through angels and revelation.
rows.anchor: ‘Din’ âdet mânasına gelir. Mânası: ‘Sizin eslâfınızdan ve şeytanlardan me’huz olan o şirk âdetiniz sizin olsun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi reads the possessive contrast as exclusive assignment of each religion to its adherent, pointing to individual responsibility for one's own deeds.
rows.anchor: İkinci mesele: لَكُمْ دِينُكُمْ hasr ifade eder, mânası sizin dininiz sizedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalili clarifies that the syntax first contrasts the two parties: your religion is yours rather than mine, and mine is mine rather than yours.
rows.anchor: Sevke nazaran izâfet tarafeyn arasında olduğu için kasırlar da “sizedir bana değil, banadır size değil” diye evvelâ tarafeyn arasında tasvir olunmak zâhirdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi infers from the opening command that the Prophet fulfilled his revealed duty; their persistence in kufr cannot harm him, and the harm belongs to them.
rows.anchor: Ben mükellef olduğum vazifemi yaptım, teklîfin uhdesinden çıktım

rows.speaker: Ebussuud
rows.claim: Ebussuud says their shirk is confined to them and cannot become the Prophet's religion; their hope that he join their worship is impossible, and his tawhid remains his.
rows.anchor: Ebussuud bunu daha vâzıh olarak şöyle tasvir etmiştir: “Sizin dininiz ki işrâkten ibarettir, o sizin için husûle maksurdur

rows.speaker: Ebussuud
rows.claim: Ebussuud treats the proposed exchange of worship as shirk because it makes both sides partners in each other's worship; the fronted predicate therefore gives a contrastive restriction.
rows.anchor: ‘bir sene sen bizim ilâhlarımıza ibadet edersen bir sene de biz senin ilâhına ibadet ederiz’ demeleri de iki tarafın iki ibadette şirketleri esasına mübtenî olduğu için

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The possessive restrictions can also reiterate the preceding refusals: only the Prophet's religion is his, not theirs, and their religion is theirs, not his.
rows.anchor: ‘Bana ancak benim dinimdir sizin dininiz değil.’

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says citing this verse as a truce formula is impermissible because revelation is for reflection and acting upon it, not merely quoting it as a proverb.
rows.anchor: Râzî der ki: “Nâsın bir mütareke sırasında bu âyet ile temessül etmeleri âdet olmuştur, bu ise câiz değildir.

rows.speaker: Âlûsî
rows.claim: Alusi objects that Razi's argument tends to close the door on Quranic quotation, which is accepted and occurs in Prophetic, Companion, imam, and Successor speech.
rows.anchor: Âlûsî buna ilişerek şöyle demiştir: “Bunda iktibas kapısını sedde bir meyil vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalili accepts quotation in suitable contexts that preserve reverence; Razi's concern is thoughtless quotation, and using the verse as a truce formula would ignore reflection and its meaning.
rows.anchor: iktibâsın cevâzı da her yerde değil, münasib ve ihtirâma münâfî olmayan mevrid ve mânalarda olabileceğini unutmamak lâzım gelir.

rows.speaker: Âlûsî
rows.claim: Alusi favors a meaning that does not require abrogation, since abrogation departs from the apparent sense and should be avoided absent necessity.
rows.anchor: Evlâ olan mensuh olmayacak bir mâna ile tefsir olunmaktır, çünkü nesh hilâf-ı zâhirdir, zarûret olmadıkça ona gidilmez.

rows.speaker: Kādî Beyzâvî
rows.claim: Baydawi says the verse neither permits unbelief nor bars jihad, so a battle verse cannot abrogate it unless it is interpreted as a truce.
rows.anchor: Kādî Beyzâvî de şöyle demiştir: “Bunda ne küfre izin ne de cihaddan men‘yoktur ki kıtal âyeti ile mensûh olsun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following al-Nasr indicates that al-Kafirun is not abrogated but belongs to the struggle that precedes victory and conquest.
rows.anchor: Bu sûreyi ber vech-i âtî Nasr Sûresi’nin tâkip etmesi de bunun mensuh olmak şöyle dursun, nasr ve fetih mukaddimâtından olan mücahede kabîlinden olduğuna işaret eder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idha is a temporal adverb expressing certainty; with past-form verbs in a conditional construction it shifts their sense to future. The condition is the combined arrival of aid and the Prophet's seeing, and the response is glorification and its coordination.
rows.anchor: اِذَا Tahakkuk ifade eder bir zarf-ı zaman olduğu için fi‘l-i mâzîye dâhil olur, şart mânasına delâlet ettiği cihetle de mâzînin mânasını müstakbele kalb ederek şartın istikbalde tahakkukunu ifade eyler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised future is that God's aid and conquest will come and Muhammad will see people enter God's religion in groups; God has promised to make His messengers prevail and to aid believers, and Muhammad's tawhid, sincere worship, and struggle fulfill the conditions for that promise.
rows.anchor: sen Allah’ın resûlü olduğun ve evvelki sûre mazmûnu üzere tevhid ve ihlâs ile Allah’a ibadet ve ubûdiyet edip sırf O’nun dinine sarıldığın, bu suretle mücahede ederek ona yardım ettiğinden dolayı bunlar muhakkak olacak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasr means God's promised assistance that makes the believers victorious over their enemies, as promised in 61:13.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın nusreti düşmanlara karşı gālib ve muzaffer kılacak olan mev‘ud yardımı

rows.speaker: Zemahşerî
rows.claim: Zamakhshari distinguishes nasr as relief and superiority over the enemy from feth as opening lands; he identifies the conquest as victory over the Arabs or Quraysh and the opening of Mecca, or generally the lands of shirk.
rows.anchor: Zemahşerî der ki: “‘Nasr’ ile ‘feth’ arasında ne fark vardır ki ona atfedilmiş? dersen, derim ki: ‘Nasr’ iğāse ve düşman üzere üstün kılmaktır

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Razi distinguishes aid that enables attainment of the desired goal from the conquest that realizes it; aid is the cause of conquest and is therefore coordinated with it.
rows.anchor: Râzî tefsirinde de der ki: “‘nasr’ matlûbun tahsîline i‘ânedir, ‘feth’ de ona

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Razi also reads aid as completion of the religion and conquest as worldly success, together making a complete blessing like the completion of religion and favor in 5:3.
rows.anchor: İkinci bir vecih: ‘Nusret’ dinin kemâli, ‘feth’ dünyevî ikbaldir ki tamamı nimettir
